pairs.reasons: Both catch all 11 planted issues and both drafts fix the tax claim, the name, the terms and the exclamation marks. A adds noise: it flags the spaced hyphen in the subject and 'Word' as violations, though the guide forbids neither. A's full rewrite also keeps 'Connect your bank and you're ready' even though A itself says that claim is unverified. B labels its non-violations as missed opportunities, drops the bank claim, adds the EUR 12 price and pillar 1, and gives a cleaner draft that is ready to ship. B's fixes follow the guide throughout. A's fixes mostly do, apart from keeping the unverified bank claim.

A misses the exclamation-mark violation (E3). Worse, under 'Checked and fine' it says the email has only one exclamation mark when it has three. A reviewer who trusts that line would ship a violation, but A's own rewrite happens to contain none. B catches all 11 issues but adds noise: an English-vs-Dutch language question rated Medium, 'Word' read as a dig at a rival, and freelancers-vs-zzp'ers. B also wrongly says the draft already uses 'btw' once. B's full revision still contains '30 seconds' with a source-needed placeholder and several bracketed notes, so it needs more editing than A's cleaner draft. Both sets of fixes follow the guide. On balance, full coverage counts for more in a pre-ship brand check.

Both catch all 11 planted issues and add the accountant line in the right place. A's suggested revision brings in new risks: a headline 'Send an invoice in minutes', a time claim with no source; 'up to 2x faster' kept behind a placeholder footnote; and the 5,000+ count kept with no source because A assumes it is accurate. B's revision drops the 2x figure, footnotes the user count, and leads with pillar 3 (Dutch-first, iDEAL, kvk-nummer). B also gives clear before/after edits and a compliance section. B's only mild over-flag is the third-person heading 'Why freelancers switch'.
